blocks.text: More than 100 million red crabs on Australia’s Christmas Island have begun their annual migration from the forest to the sea, conservationists said this week. The yearly march of the crabs on the remote territory in the Indian Ocean comes when the rainy season hits and the crustaceans move to the sea to breed. Lunar cycles decide the timing of their epic migration through forests, across roads and over bridges. The crabs hope to spawn “before dawn on a receding high tide during the moon’s last quarter”, Parks Australia said. 291st Feast of Nuestra Señora de Regla: Key dates and activities […]...
